claim: Direct-classifier thresholds were selected only from track-disjoint validation OOF predictions; frozen evaluation was not used for threshold reselection.
The direct classifier improves balanced accuracy across TestReal and Fresh WildBox at both horizons.
basis: All four track-cluster 95% CIs for balanced-accuracy delta are above zero.

claim: The direct classifier substantially improves crossing sensitivity across all four evaluation conditions.
basis: All four sensitivity-delta 95% CIs are above zero.

claim: The sensitivity gain has a false-positive cost: false-positive rate increases across all four conditions.
basis: All four FPR-delta 95% CIs are above zero.

claim: The direct classifier is less precise than the nominal crossing rule in all four conditions.
basis: All four precision-delta 95% CIs are below zero.

claim: F1 improves on both TestReal horizons and Fresh WildBox 5s, but Fresh WildBox 2s F1 improvement is uncertain.
basis: Fresh 2s F1 CI crosses zero; the other three exclude zero.

claim: The direct classifier provides a useful higher-sensitivity operating point for virtual-geofence crossing detection.
basis: Balanced accuracy/sensitivity rise, but FPR rises and precision falls.

claim: The direct classifier is universally better than the nominal crossing rule.
basis: Trade-offs remain: higher FPR and lower precision in every condition.

claim: The direct classifier reduces false alarms relative to the nominal rule.
basis: Observed FPR deltas are positive with CIs above zero.

claim: Report the direct classifier as a secondary decision-layer benchmark/ablation, not a replacement for primary Step7H RED/YELLOW/GREEN logic.
basis: Step7H remains the locked primary operational protocol.
